From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 07:12:00 -0800
Subject: Zephyrus12b — elevated 5xx window detected

Heads up — automated alerts picked up an elevated 5xx and timeout window for Zephyrus12b in us-west-2. Summary: 07:00–07:30 PST we observed a 5xx rate of ~4.8% and median generation time increased from 210ms to ~1.2s for requests with seq<=1024. Error mix is ~60% 502 gateway and ~40% internal 5xx.

What I've captured so far: 
- Correlated to a rollout of a new kernel selector on the serving fleet (canary subset).
- KV cache hit rate dropped ~12% during the window.
- Autoscaler did not trigger additional capacity until 07:18 (race with rollout).

Attachments: zephyrus_error_window.csv, zephyrus_stacktrace.log (stack traces sampled at 07:08/07:14).

Asks: please triage routing and decide whether to engage customer now. Connor, can you validate whether fallback routing to the legacy kernel is available for the affected pool? Jordan — recommend we notify Acme Ops and Alice if we confirm customer impact.

— Neha

Subject: RE: Zephyrus12b — elevated 5xx window detected

Alice — I'm Jordan on the account team at Redwood. Quick update: our SREs detected a transient surge of 5xx/timeouts affecting Zephyrus12b between ~07:00–07:30 PST. We are seeing increased 5xx and higher tail latencies for shorter-context requests.

Immediate mitigation we executed (07:20–07:35 PST):
- Rolled back the kernel selector change on the canary subset; fallback routing to the prior kernel is in place.
- Redirected a portion of Acme traffic to Zephyrus-lite (compatible variant) to keep throughput steady while we validate stability.
- Restarted two misbehaving workers in the affected pool.

Current status: errors have dropped to baseline (<=0.2%), and latency distribution returned to expected. Connor and Neha are continuing post-incident verification. We plan a short post-incident call to walk through timeline and next steps — propose Sun 12/20 10:00 PST; please let us know if that works.

I'll attach a short CSV and the stack trace sample for your engineering team. Full RCA will follow once we've finished log correlation and replay checks.

Attachments: zephyrus_error_window.csv, zephyrus_stacktrace.log

Thanks and sorry for the disruption — we take stability seriously and will follow up with a full timeline and root cause.

Subject: Zephyrus12b incident 2026-12-19 — recovery confirmation & RCA plan

Alice / Acme Ops — thanks again for joining the call. This thread will be the reference for follow-up. Quick closure notes and the plan for RCA: 

1) Incident summary (concise):
- Incident window: 2026-12-19T07:00:00-08:00 PST (elevated 5xx/timeouts, peak 4.8% at 07:12).
- Impacted model: Zephyrus12b (primary serving pool in us-west-2).
- Root trigger (preliminary): a kernel selector rollout on a canary subset caused degraded KV cache behavior and raised contention on worker threads under specific input token distributions.

2) Actions taken during mitigation:
- Immediate rollback of kernel selector change (07:20 PST).
- Partial traffic failover to Zephyrus-lite (07:25 PST) for safety while we validated stability.
- Worker restarts and cache invalidation on affected nodes (07:28–07:35).

3) Current state:
- Baseline behaviour restored by 07:40 PST; post-verification checks completed.
- No data retention or data exfiltration concerns identified.

4) Planned RCA deliverables and timeline:
- Interim one-page summary (this thread) — delivered.
- Full RCA with logs, timelines, and corrective actions — ETA 2026-12-22 18:00 PST (link will be shared to Drive and Jira INC-4821).
- Preventive work: add a pre-deploy KV-cache stress gate to our kernel selector rollout process, plus expanded canary percentage checks. Target for rollout by 2027-01-10.

5) SLA / credits: Connor will open an internal billing review and correlate uptime windows with your contract to confirm whether the event meets SLA credit criteria (we will provide incident ID and the billing window).

Attached: acme_request_form.pdf (completed), zephyrus_error_window.csv, zephyrus_stacktrace.log.

Next steps: Connor (cc) will post the Jira ticket with the final RCA and link to the Drive doc. Jordan will follow up on scheduling a retro with your infra leads if you'd like deeper technical review.

Appreciate your patience — we'll keep the communication tight until RCA delivery.
